# Player guide

Requires Warcraft III 3.0 and a keyboard; nothing else to install. Download the map from [Hive Workshop](https://www.hiveworkshop.com/threads/makgora.375492/), put it in the Warcraft III Maps folder and open it from Custom Games.

A controller is optional: the Mak'gora controller helper turns its buttons and sticks into its own pad keys, which work with any Controls layout. The default Melee pad layout uses A to attack, B for specials, X/Y to jump, RB to grab and LB for Strong; Tom's pad layout uses A to attack, X for specials, Y to jump, B to grab, LB to short hop and RB for Strong. In both, either trigger shields or air-dodges and Start pauses.

The game has character and stage selection, 16 fighters, computer opponents, floating platforms, blast zones, stocks, rematches and configurable controls. Every fighter's specials and ultimate are listed by name in the [move list](move-list.md). More fighters are in the Forge, still in development: turn on Forge in the Match Rules to see them.

## Keyboard controls

WASD is the default layout. Change it on the Controls screen (F2 at fighter select).

| Action | WASD | Box | Custom |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Left | A | W | W |
| Right | D | R | R |
| Up | W | P | SPACE |
| Down | S | E | E |
| Jump | 8 | 8 | 9 |
| Short hop | I | I | I |
| Attack | N | N | N |
| Special | U | U | U |
| Strong (smash) | 9 | 9 | 0 |
| Grab | O | O | O |
| Shield | Q | Q | Q |
| Second shield | 7 | 7 | 8 |
| Light shield | E | A | A |
| Walk (Mod X) | SPACE | SPACE | P |
| Tilt (Mod Y) | C | C | ; |
| C-up | Y | Y | Y |
| C-left | J | J | J |
| C-down | K | K | K |
| C-right | L | L | L |

## Getting started

For solo practice, place only your own fighter chip and press Y, then choose a stage and press Y again. Leave the CPU chip unplaced. Practice has no timer or opponent, and falling off the stage respawns you without ending the session. Place the CPU chip before starting when you want a match against the computer.

Below each CPU card, Opponent settings lets you choose Rook, Ember, Flint, Vale, Kite or Wren, then Peon, Grunt or Warchief difficulty. Each opponent has recognizable tendencies and improves several skills as difficulty rises. The preview describes that exact opponent and difficulty, including an opening to watch for. New CPU slots start with Wren at Grunt. The first player or the slot owner can change the choices; everyone else can read the preview. Random chooses an opponent each match and keeps your difficulty. Choices stay through fighter or stage changes, New Match and automatic rematches.

New players can open the Tutorial at fighter select: 10 short lessons with a training partner (Move and dash, Jump and double jump, Attacks, Specials, Ultimate orbs, Ultimate, Shield and dodge, Grab and throw, Get back to the ledge, Knock out your partner). Pick any lesson to play it again.

## Rules

At fighter selection, the rules pill in the middle of the top bar shows the rules; click it (or move the menu focus to it and press Attack) to open the rules drawer, where any player can change Stocks, Time, Ultimates, Items, Endless, Automatic rematch and Forge, pick a preset (Tourney, Party, Endless) or Reset default. Hover a rule to read what it does.

Team Battle: choose each fighter’s red, blue, teal or purple team. At least two teams must join; the last team standing wins.

Stocks: how many times each fighter can be knocked off the stage before they lose.

Time limit: the match ends when it runs out. Lower it to “No time limit” to play until stocks run out.

Endless play: no stocks are lost and there is no timer. Fight freely; pause, then hold Esc for a second (or hold L, R and A and press Start) to leave.

Automatic rematch: when a match ends, the same fighters and rules start again after a short countdown.

Forge: also show the fighters and stages still in development, marked with a hammer, on every player’s character and stage select. Random, computer picks and Arcade use finished fighters only.

Items: a power-up appears at centre stage every 30–60 s after a 10 s countdown. Touch it and press Attack to grab it.

Ultimates: with a full meter bar, Attack + Special unleashes your fighter's ultimate. The bar fills from the match clock: full 60 s after the start and after each use. With Orbs on, only the orb that appears above centre stage every 30 s fills it, half a bar each. Off: no ultimates; Attack + Special is the ordinary special.

## Training

Training (the mode list at the top left) turns the match into practice against computer partners: no clock and no lost stocks. Choose what the partner does (Stand, Shield, Crouch, Jump, Attack or Fight), which way it drifts when hit, how it techs, its damage, whether hit areas show (bodies green, attacks red) and the speed (Full, Half or Quarter). Fight uses the partner's chosen opponent and difficulty.

The top-left readout gives your last attack's frames, how many frames ahead (+) or behind (-) you were after it hit or was shielded, and the combo. Hold both shields and press Attack (Q + 7 + N on WASD) to put everyone back at the start.

An orange halo means your fighter is locked and no current input can help. A green halo means moving the stick can change the hit or throw, while buttons cannot. The halo disappears as soon as a button can matter, including an attack you can queue before recovery or a tech you can press before landing.

## Menus

Mouse buttons and your left/right keys + N (your Attack key) select a fighter or stage; U (Special) goes back. Menus always follow your own bindings, and the arrow keys work too. Drag a character chip from the active player card onto the roster. New Match keeps selections. On the selection screens Y confirms and chooses the next match after a result. While the Warcraft chat box is open, typing never pauses, moves or attacks. Enter is reserved for Warcraft chat.

At fighter selection, up/down moves focus between fighter cards and CPU Opponent settings. Left/right changes the focused fighter; Attack opens focused settings. Inside the panel, up/down visits Opponent, Difficulty and Done; left/right changes the value. Attack advances to the next row or chooses Done, and Special or Close returns while keeping choices. Controller menus use the left stick to move the pointer, A to choose and B to go back.

The title screen opens from fighter selection with the < MENU button at the top left, Esc, or by moving the menu focus down to it and pressing Attack.

## Pause

Esc or Backspace pauses or resumes an active match (Start on a controller). Pausing freezes combat and match time. The pause screen keeps the frozen match in view: the stick (your movement keys on a keyboard) pans the camera and the C-stick zooms, on your own screen only, and the view snaps back when the match resumes.

To leave, hold two shield buttons and Attack, then press Start (Esc or Backspace), or click the RESET MATCH plate at the bottom right. The player who paused can also hold Esc for one second to fill the bar above the plate; a tap still resumes. Leaving a match always goes to fighter selection.

The pause screen lists its keys: F2 shows or hides the in-game controls, and F10 opens the Warcraft menu.

## The Controls screen

Every game opens on the Controls screen, one for each player, before fighter select. The top row holds WASD (recommended if you're new), Box (the leverless controller style) and, once you customize a layout, your selected Custom slot; picking one saves it as your profile. Rebinding a key on WASD or Box copies that layout into a new Custom profile (WASD - custom1, Box - custom1, and so on), selects it and saves it.

Click a lit key to rebind, or click its red x to clear. Press the new key for the flashing action. Delete clears it, Escape cancels. If another action already held that key, the two swap; Save keeps the layout. Rename names the Custom slot; Reset brings back the Custom defaults. The bottom row holds Show controls in game, Stick Jump (off by default: when on, pressing Up jumps) and C-Stick Tilt Attack (on by default: when off, the C-stick gives uncharged smashes on the ground and aerials in the air), with Save and Done on the right.

Done (or Escape) closes the screen; each player confirms their own. F2 opens it again before a match. Type -save in chat to save your controls and delay, or -load to bring them back. Backspace and Escape are reserved for pause; F1, F2, F5, F6 and F7 are reserved too, and the screen names why if you try one.

In a match, a CONTROLS panel between the player panels lists every action with its key and lights a row while you hold it. Press F2 in a match to hide or show it; the choice is saved with your controls.

## Help and bug reports

Type -help (or -commands) in chat for every player command, or press F9 for the quest log's Controls, How to play and Commands entries (listed below).

Saw something wrong? Type -clip in chat, or hold View on a controller for a second: the last ten seconds of the match are saved in Warcraft III's CustomMapData folder as makgora-repro-*.txt, and "Moment saved" appears. The match goes on undisturbed.

Use Warcraft's ordinary Quit Mission to leave and recreate a custom game. The Ctrl+R restart path is unreliable, and F5 has hung the client when returning to the menu.

## Moving, attacking and grabbing

Shield + Attack, or Grab (O on WASD), grabs. While holding an opponent, tap Attack to pummel or push a direction to throw. Mash buttons and alternate directions to escape a grab; holding one button does not count. The bar above a held fighter drains as the hold runs out.

Short hop (I on every keyboard layout; LB in Tom's pad layout) always short hops, however long you hold it. The ordinary jump keys full hop when held and short hop when released during startup. In the air, Short hop uses your second jump.

Attacks buffer for six frames, including through jump squat. Two modifiers shape the stick (Tom's design, 2026-10-30). Walk (Mod X) reduces the horizontal value only: it walks, gives forward tilts, and with up and a side sends a steep up-diagonal. Tilt (Mod Y) reduces the vertical value only: it gives up and down tilts and shallow diagonals. Hold both for the all-purpose tilt.

Attack with a direction performs a tilt when standing, walking or crouching; out of a dash or a run it is the dash attack. The C-stick keys always give the tilt they name on the ground, even out of a dash or a run, and the aerials in the air.

Strong (9 on WASD and Box, 0 on Custom, LB or RB on a pad) gives the smashes, after Rivals of Aether's strong button. Strong never attacks on its own: Strong + a direction is that direction's smash, and Strong + Attack on the ground is always the up smash. Keep holding to charge it. In the air, Strong + Attack with a direction gives that aerial.

Hold down while rising into a platform without an aerial to stand on it at once. Release down, then press it hard again to drop through a platform. Press down again in the air to fast-fall.

To moonwalk, dash and then tilt the stick lightly backward: your fighter keeps facing forward while it slides back. On a keyboard, hold down together with the back key.

After a landing with landing lag, a direction you kept holding walks out when the lag ends; pressing a direction fresh buffers a dash that way.

## Specials and ultimates

Specials use Special (U on WASD) with a direction. Strong + Special with a direction is the same special. At a full ultimate meter, Attack + Special together is your fighter's ultimate (A + B in the Melee pad layout, A + X in Tom's); below a full meter it is the plain special. The Ultimates rule above explains how the meter fills.

## Modes

Versus: fight players and computers with the rules on this screen.

Training: practise on a partner you set up; no stocks or timer.

Arcade: a fixed run of eight fights that ends on your rival. The Horde won the world, and now every race fights up through the war bands for the right to challenge the Warchief.

## How to play

Stocks: each fighter has a few lives (stocks). Hits raise damage %, and the higher it is the farther a hit sends you. Fly past the edge of the screen and you lose a stock; the last fighter with stocks wins.

Shield: hold your shield key to block. The bubble shrinks while held and breaks if it gets too small, leaving you dizzy. Shield in the air to air-dodge.

Recovery: knocked off the stage, use your second jump, then Up + Special to fly back. Grab the ledge to hang on, then press a direction or jump to get up.

## Training settings

Partner: what the training partner does: stand, shield, crouch, jump, attack or fight back.

Partner drift: which way the partner steers while it flies from your hits.

Partner tech: whether and where the partner breaks its fall when it hits the ground.

Partner damage: the partner's starting damage. Higher damage sends it flying farther.

Hit areas: draw where every attack hits and where every fighter can be hit.

Game speed: slow the whole game to half or quarter speed to study moves.

Speed item: for 10 s you run and drift ×1.3 faster and jump higher. You glow cyan in a whirlwind.

Heavy item: for 10 s you turn to iron: knockback you take ÷1.5 and you fall faster.

## Tutorial lessons (keys shown for WASD)

Move and dash: Push left or right (A or D) to walk. Tap it quickly to dash.

Jump and double jump: Press jump (8), then press it again in the air to jump a second time. I, or LB in Tom's pad layout, always short hops, even held.

Attacks: Walk up to your partner and press attack (N). Hold a direction to change the attack; hold strong (9) as well for a smash.

Specials: Every fighter has four specials, and they are free. Press special (U) alone for the neutral special, or with A or D for the side special, W for the up special and S for the down special. Try all four.

Ultimate orbs: The thin bar under your damage is your ultimate meter. By default it fills on the match clock, one full bar every 60 seconds; with the Orbs rule on, only orbs fill it, one appearing above centre stage every 30 seconds. Here an orb hangs there now, and each fills half the bar. Touch the orb, or hit it with a normal attack, to take it. Specials, air dodges and ultimates pass through it. Take two.

Ultimate: With a full meter your fighter glows gold. Hold attack (N) and press special (U) to fire your ultimate, and hit your partner with it. Take orbs until the bar is full.

Shield and dodge: Q: full shield; E: light shield. Q + A or D rolls; Q + S dodges. Tap Q before landing to tech; hold A or D to tech roll.

Grab and throw: Stand next to your partner and press grab (O). Then push a direction to throw.

Get back to the ledge: Jump off, then double jump (8) and up special (W + U) to the ledge. W or toward the stage climbs; 8 leaps; Q rolls; N strikes; S or away lets go.

Knock out your partner: Your partner is badly hurt. Hit it hard to knock it off the screen.

## Commands

-help or -commands: show this list of commands.

-save: save your current controls and delay as your profile for next time.

-load: load your saved profile.

F2: open the Controls screen at fighter select, or show and hide the controls panel in a match. F9: help (Controls, How to play, Commands).

Y: start from fighter or stage select (in a match Y is C-up by default). Esc or Backspace (Start on a controller): pause. -clip: save the last ten seconds of a match for a bug report.
